content.title: Noble Gas Transport in Argon Cover Gas Conditions for Alfred Lead Cooled Fast Reactor
content.abstract: Controlled injections of krypton and xenon were performed in a thermally stratified argon atmosphere to investigate noble gas transport relevant to cover gas monitoring in lead-cooled fast reactors (LFR). Experiments were conducted in the NOGATILL facility using impulse and continuous injection modes, while gas composition was monitored in real time using a quadrupole mass spectrometer. Detection delays ranged from several minutes to tens of minutes depending on injection conditions and carrier gas flow.
